record.original_question: For a smooth algebraic variety W, a point w in W, and an affine good Zariski neighborhood U of w whose universal cover U_tilde is a Stein manifold topologically equivalent to a cell, what is the complex-analytic structure of U_tilde? Is U_tilde a domain in C^n, where n=dim_C W, and can every point w have such a good neighborhood whose universal cover is a bounded domain?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $W$ be a smooth complex algebraic variety of complex dimension $n$. For a point $w \in W$, define a good Zariski neighborhood of $w$ to be an affine Zariski-open subset $U \subset W$ containing $w$ such that the universal covering $\widetilde{U}$ of $U$ is a Stein manifold that is topologically equivalent to (homeomorphic to) a cell, i.e. to $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$.

Address the following:

(a) Describe the complex-analytic structure of $\widetilde{U}$. In particular, determine whether $\widetilde{U}$ is necessarily biholomorphic to a domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$.

(b) Show whether every point $w \in W$ admits a good Zariski neighborhood $U$ in the above sense whose universal cover $\widetilde{U}$ is biholomorphic to a bounded domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$.
artifact.status_search_result: Griffiths proved that any smooth projective variety has a Zariski-open subset whose universal cover is a bounded domain of holomorphy in C^n, which gives a positive answer in the projective case for the existence of good neighborhoods with bounded universal covers. The full local question—whether every point of an arbitrary smooth algebraic variety admits such a good Zariski neighborhood, and the precise complex-analytic classification of these universal covers—does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature reviewed.

status_evidence.title: Function theory of finite order on algebraic varieties (Griffiths)
status_evidence.snippet: Universal covers of good Zariski-open sets are bounded domains of holomorphy in C^n.
status_evidence.claim: Griffiths constructed Zariski-open subsets of smooth projective varieties whose universal covers are bounded domains in C^n, providing a positive answer in the projective setting.

status_evidence.title: Coverings of Algebraic Varieties (Sendai 1985)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of universal coverings of Zariski-open subsets and their complex analytic structure.
status_evidence.claim: Related work has studied complex-analytic structure of universal covers of Zariski-open subsets of algebraic varieties.
